defects.summary: The doctor models only two of `may_replace`'s three clauses - it never compares the bytes on disk against the digest the LOCK names - and the omission produces a FALSE GREEN: an in-lock directory in a store with no readable record is reported at exit 0 with FINDINGS (0) while the hook refuses it and the session verdict reads DEGRADED. The comment that justifies the silence states the opposite of what the hook does.
defects.evidence: classify's UNKNOWN arm, check_provenance.py:1315-1319: `elif in_lock: # UNKNOWN and locked. Nothing to say that the absent record has not already said store-wide: the hook will replace it, ... continue`. Measured on HEAD with the suite's own helpers (ephemeral, store holding `alpha` with hand-placed bytes, NO record file, lock naming alpha with a digest the directory does not match): `hook_may_replace(store, "alpha", locked, ())` returns REFUSE - so the run lists alpha after `DEGRADED ... shadowed` and 0/1 is delivered - while the doctor prints `provenance: 1 on disk, 1 unattributable (no readable record) ... 0 findings`, `FINDINGS (0)`, exit 0. Same shape with a record present but not naming alpha correctly raises `hand-placed-over-locked` at exit 1; the only difference is whether a record file exists, which changes nothing about what the hook will do. This is the same class as the round-3 blocking defect - a false green over exactly the DEGRADED verdict skills-doctor exists to explain - and it is a comment asserting hook behaviour that round 4 was chartered to audit, sitting three lines below a branch 9fd29b5 rewrote. `git blame` puts it at d64667b (round 3), so round 4 did not introduce it, it walked past it. The fix needs `read_lock` (:891-896) to stop discarding the per-skill digest values it already parses: it builds `names` from the keys and drops the digests, so `Lock` carries no way to ask may_replace's second question.

defects.summary: The mirror image of the same omission, and a FALSE RED: `hand-placed-over-locked` prints HOOK_REFUSAL as a flat assertion over a store where `may_replace` returns TRUE, the hook installs normally and the verdict is OK. defects.evidence: Measured on HEAD (ephemeral; store holds `alpha`, a record that is present and names no install, a lock naming alpha whose digest is alpha's current digest): `hook_may_replace(store, "alpha", locked, ())` -> REPLACE, and the doctor exits 1 with `[hand-placed-over-locked] alpha ... The hook does not overwrite a directory it cannot show it installed unchanged: the next session start copies nothing here, leaves these bytes exactly as they are, and names this directory after `DEGRADED` in the session's `skills:` verdict as shadowed, so the locked copy is not delivered for as long as this holds.` Every clause of that is false here. The sentence that follows names the exception ("The single exception is bytes that already digest to exactly what the lock names") but does not tell the reader they are IN it, and the report still exits 1 over a healthy store. This is measurable with what the lock file already contains - `test_the_hook_does_overwrite_the_bytes_it_already_ships` (test_check_provenance.py:3755-3768) calls `hook_may_replace(store, "alpha", pristine, ())` with `recorded=()`, i.e. the record naming nothing, which IS the UNATTRIBUTED input shape, and asserts REPLACE - so the suite proves the hook replaces here while the doctor's output for that shape is never run. Reachable whenever a developer hand-copies the registry's own bytes into a store whose record was written without that name (e.g. after a record rewrite that forgot earlier installs).

defects.summary: `digest_shared_payload`'s docstring forbids in capitals the exact use its only in-file caller makes of it - judging a copy against a RECORDED digest - and the caller is the ARTEFACTS_ONLY test. The code is sound; the prohibition is now false about the file it lives in.
defects.evidence: check_provenance.py:512-516: "For COMPARING two copies of one skill with each other, and for nothing else. Never for judging a copy against a RECORDED digest: the record and the lock both carry `digest_skill_dir`'s answer over the whole directory, so using this against one of those would report edited bytes as unchanged - precisely the lie `_cause` exists to avoid telling." check_provenance.py:1362: `elif digest_shared_payload(skills_dir / name) == entry.digest:` - `entry.digest` is the recorded digest. The inference is actually valid (both functions emit the same `<relpath>\0<sha256>\n` manifest, so the equality means the uploaded-file subset now equals the whole file set at install), which is why nothing breaks - but a reader who takes the docstring at face value must conclude the ARTEFACTS_ONLY branch is the bug it warns about. `git log -S` puts the docstring at 1359106 and the caller at bb7056e (round 3); round 4 rewrote the messages either side of :1362 and both artefact findings without reconciling it.

defects.summary: `dropped_files`' docstring justifies its empty-list contract with a case that cannot reach either caller, and the `if extra else ''` guard both callers carry is therefore dead.
defects.evidence: check_provenance.py:483-486: "Empty is a real answer as well as a failure answer: the difference can be a dropped file that was there at install and is not now, in which case there is nothing left to name." Both callers (:1377 and :1418) are guarded by `integrity == ARTEFACTS_ONLY`, which requires `digest_shared_payload(dir) == entry.digest` AND `digest_skill_dir(dir) != entry.digest`. If `dropped_files(dir)` were empty then every file is in the uploaded set, so `digest_shared_payload(dir) == digest_skill_dir(dir)`, which makes `digest_skill_dir(dir) == entry.digest` and the earlier UNCHANGED branch takes it instead; if `uploaded_files` fails, `digest_shared_payload` returns None and ARTEFACTS_ONLY is not reached either. Measured: a hook-installed `alpha` recorded WITH a `__pycache__/x.pyc` present and the artefact deleted since routes to `[edited-and-locked]` at exit 1, never to an artefacts finding. So the named case is real for the function and unreachable for its only uses, and `{' (' + name_list(extra) + ')' if extra else ''}` never takes its empty arm.
